findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or absent file path aborts the entire process with a panic instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? to propagate the error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value in the second field
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV data aborts the entire session load with a panic instead of skipping or reporting the bad record
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(...) or .ok_or(...) with a domain parse error, then propagate via Result

findings.problem: as u16 cast after parse silently truncates values outside u16 range (0..=65535)
findings.failure_mode: A value like 70000 in the CSV silently wraps to 4464, corrupting data without any error indication
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed) and propagate the TryFromError as a typed domain error

findings.problem: parts[0] accesses index 0 without bounds check; if a line is empty this will panic
findings.failure_mode: An empty line or whitespace-only line triggers an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of being gracefully skipped or reported
findings.fix: Use parts.first().copied() or get(0) and map to a Result or Option

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() accesses index 0 without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: Same empty-line panic as line 16; duplicated unchecked access

findings.problem: parts[1] accesses index 1 without bounds check; a single-field line panics here
findings.failure_mode: A line with only a name (no comma) triggers index-out-of-bounds panic instead of a parse error
findings.fix: Use .get(1) and map to a domain error indicating the value field is missing

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(...).collect() allocates a Vec of all parts when only two are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per line; also masks the intent that exactly two fields are expected, so malformed lines with extra fields are silently accepted
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').map_err(...) and handle the two-field case directly without collect

findings.problem: println!() is a side effect hidden inside a data-loading/parsing function that returns pure data
findings.failure_mode: I/O side effects are mixed into the functional core, making the function non-deterministic, impossible to test in isolation, and producing observable output even when the caller only wants data
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core. If logging is needed, return a status/warning alongside Record or push it into the imperative shell layer

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string performs file I/O directly inside the function; no separation of parsing from I/O
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be unit-tested with synthetic data without mocking the filesystem; the I/O and parsing concerns are inseparable
findings.fix: Split into load_sessions_from(path: &str) -> Result<String, io::Error> for the shell layer and parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> for the pure core

findings.problem: Vec<Record> is returned via .collect() with no bounded allocation handling; allocation failure is silently OOM-killed
findings.failure_mode: A very large file causes uncontrolled allocation that can OOM the process instead of returning a controlled error the caller can act on
findings.fix: Use try_reserve before collecting, or return Result<Vec<Record>, AllocationError> and handle try_reserve failures

findings.problem: println! is a visible I/O side effect in a function whose signature promises only data return (Vec<Record>)
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot suppress output; the function produces side effects invisible from its type signature, violating the imperative-shell boundary
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely; log at the shell boundary or return a diagnostic alongside the records

findings.problem: use std::fs; imports filesystem I/O at the module level, signaling the module is not a pure functional core
findings.failure_mode: Signals architectural confusion between shell and core; any downstream reader may assume this module can handle I/O
findings.fix: Move fs::read_to_string call to a shell-layer function; the core should only accept &str or &[u8]

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions throughput or allocation behavior
no profiler data exists to show allocation hotspots (split+collect, String::to_string per part)
no allocation tracing evidence (e.g., alloc_counter, mimalloc stats) for bounded-growth verification
no second-ring verification (Miri for UB, Kani for arithmetic bounds, or proptest for malformed CSV inputs)
no command evidence that cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test were executed
residual_risk: This single function has 12 Holzman violations including 3 unwrap panics, 3 unchecked index accesses, 1 lossy cast, 1 split+collect anti-pattern, 2 functional-core I/O breaches, and 1 missing try_reserve. The code cannot safely handle any untrusted input without panicking. No benchmarks, Miri, Kani, or test evidence exists. The entire function must be rewritten with typed error propagation, split_once parsing, checked conversions, and I/O separated into a shell layer before any deployment is possible.
